page_title: MD Preview — Follow Local Markdown Without Opening an IDE

summary.name: MD Preview
summary.one_liner: A lightweight Rust desktop and Android app for previewing and lightly editing local Markdown and text files in tabs, built on the system WebView instead of Electron.
use_cases: Reading plans, READMEs, and generated reports without opening an IDE
Following links between local Markdown notes
Quickly editing and saving a Markdown file
Exporting a clean PDF from a Markdown document
Previewing Mermaid diagrams and KaTeX math offline
summary.what_it_does: MD Preview opens local Markdown and text files in tabs within a single window, and reopens the same tab order and active document after a restart without caching document bodies. Relative and absolute links to local Markdown or text files open in tabs, while missing or unsupported targets leave the current preview intact. It renders code with 40+ highlight.js languages, KaTeX formulas, Mermaid diagrams, tables, and alerts offline. Users can toggle a source editor, which autosaves after a short pause, and can print or export the preview to PDF. It also shows live character counts, content-only zoom, and search within the rendered preview with Cmd/Ctrl+F.
notable: Uses the system WebView (WebView2 on Windows, WebKitGTK on Linux) instead of bundling Chromium; about 5MB binary and about 15MB memory per the page
Follows local Markdown and text links and opens them in tabs
Works offline with Mermaid, KaTeX, and highlight.js rendering
caveats: macOS, iOS, and iPadOS downloads are currently unavailable
Pricing and license are not stated on the page
Performance figures are the project's own comparison against Electron-based apps
